scope: Capability parity inventory against documented LuaJIT FFI, not a claim of a drop-in ffi module or completed parity. Pending implementation may move after this baseline.

statusMeaning.partial: Existing test proves only the named Nupp subset; remaining acceptance scenario is not satisfied.
statusMeaning.pending: No VM acceptance evidence for this capability at baseline.
statusMeaning.validated: Reserved for full declared scenario passing all required applicable modes/targets; no entries promoted from code inspection alone.

targetMatrix: additional supported ABI targets require their own evidence
acceptancePolicy.nativeOracle: ffi/fixture.c must be built independently and called from Nupp; a Python/C oracle run alone is not Nupp FFI acceptance.
acceptancePolicy.memory: GC stress/oracle for managed owners, callbacks, namespace lifetimes and native return values; tests never intentionally dereference invalid pointers.
acceptancePolicy.performance: Keep feature correctness separate from compiled coverage and dispatch overhead. LuaJIT interpreter fallback features still belong in capability parity.
acceptancePolicy.persistence: Managed pointers/views must preserve aliases; external libraries/functions/pointers need explicit rebind/resource policy and must never serialize process addresses.

knownSemanticDifferences: Nupp exact numeric equality and interned numeric keys differ from LuaJIT cast-before-compare and object-identity cdata keys. Do not change core Nupp semantics implicitly to mimic ffi.
Nupp managed views retain owners and bounds; LuaJIT raw pointers are untraced/unbounded. Separate managed storage from explicit external native pointers.
Lua-only userdata/lightuserdata/FILE* carriers and LuaJIT-specific ABI flags require documented equivalents or compatibility API scope.

luajitUnsupported.limit: No integrated C preprocessor except pragma pack; prepare headers externally.
Obscure C constant expressions beyond documented parser support need not match.
No implicit int or K&R unprototyped functions; f() means zero parameters.
long double parses but conversions, access and arithmetic unsupported.
Wide-character string and character literals unsupported; wchar_t type itself exists.
static const limited to integer types up to32bits; string/float constants unsupported.
Packed bitfields crossing storage-container boundaries unsupported.
Vectors load/store/initialize and lane read only; general arithmetic unsupported.
Compiled LuaJIT ignores volatile; stronger Nupp semantics may be implemented independently.
Complex storage/conversion supported; complex arithmetic unsupported.
Passing structs by value to variadic C functions unsupported.
Callbacks cannot be variadic or take/return by-value aggregates.
Compiled LuaJIT FFI calls back into Lua are disallowed; interpreter routing required.
C++ exception interoperability does not cover compiled FFI calls.

luajitInterpreterOnly: non-default VLA/VLS or large initialization (>128bytes or>16arrayelements)
pointer differences with non-power-of-two element sizes
ctype __newindex tables and nonstring __index table lookup

rust.scope: Scalar widths, exact wide integers, promoted varargs, errno, managed-pointer private owners under public and source metadata mutation plus GC, forged/growable-owner rejection, readonly signature admission and mutable string rejection, external-pointer persistence rejection, natural HFA/large and semantic boolean/integer aggregate copy semantics, C union layout and pointer overlay, and union/nested-union by-value signature rejection.

acceptedSlice: bool, signed/unsigned 8/16/32/64-bit scalar C calls; exact wide values
binary32/binary64 C calls including rounding, signed zero, infinity and NaN
nil and managed native pointers, copied NUL-terminated native strings and embedded-NUL copy
natural struct by-value HFA arguments/return and 32-byte hidden return ABI
missing symbol, invalid signature, arity, and closed-handle errors
scalar callback allocation/GC, native reentry, retention, replacement, error recovery, bool/uint64/double returns
AOT scalar/pointer/vararg/aggregate calls in three fresh processes with executable memory denied
Mutable native signatures reject readonly views; readonly pointer descriptors admit them
Forged storage dictionaries and marked views over growable owners are rejected
Returned pointers privately root physical owners even after source view metadata is removed
Natural union C size/alignment/offset/pointer overlay; direct and nested union by-value signatures explicitly rejected
Callbacks can close the active binding and a pointer with a closed parent, force GC, and return safely while C still reads the retained owner
Callbacks can close an aggregate-return binding and force GC while its otherwise unreachable result descriptor remains valid
Semantic boolean/integer struct fields match independent C _Bool/int32 by-value layout and copy semantics
Managed strings and slices require readonly pointer parameter descriptors
limits: Only aarch64 macOS has this native ABI execution evidence; other platforms remain pending.
Callbacks are excluded from the no-executable-memory gate because libffi closures allocate executable code.
Pointer/aggregate/variadic callback signatures, by-value unions, native globals, finalizers, metatypes and the remaining baseline inventory are not accepted by this slice.
The original Tecs snapshot benchmark remains a separate uncompleted integration.
